title: CofCA: A STEP-WISE Counterfactual Multi-hop QA benchmark

contributions.purpose: Enable evaluation of LLMs' real multi-step reasoning ability on multi-hop QA while disentangling genuine reasoning from memorized internal knowledge / data contamination in Wikipedia-based benchmarks.
contributions.mechanism: CofCA, a step-wise counterfactual MHQA benchmark: a human-in-the-loop pipeline where GPT-4 rewrites Wikipedia passages into counterfactual passages (keyword replacement + paraphrasing, human-reviewed) and generates multi-hop QA plus sub-QA pairs; paired with an equal amount of factual MHQA control data from HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, MuSiQue. Includes step-wise reasoning-chain (sub-question) evaluation.
contributions.evaluation: 900 counterfactual items (2/3/4-hop) + 900 factual items (300 each from HotpotQA/2Wiki/MuSiQue); inter-annotator agreement 94% overall (96/92/95% for 2/3/4-hop); quality also scored by GPT-4 for correctness/informativeness.
contributions.source_quote: To address these issues, we introducea Step-wise Counterfactual benchmark (CofCA), a novel evaluation benchmark consisting of factual data and counterfactual data that reveals LLMs' real reasoning abilities on multi-step reasoning and reasoning chain evaluation.

contributions.purpose: Expose that reported LLM multi-hop QA performance is inflated by data contamination, quantifying the gap between factual (Wikipedia) and counterfactual data.
contributions.mechanism: Comparative evaluation of proprietary (GPT-4, GPT-3.5, text-davinci-003, Bing Chat, Gemini-pro) and open-source (Llama2-7b, Mistral-7b, Qwen-7b) LLMs on factual vs counterfactual splits, using EM/F1 and GPT-4-turbo partial-match (PM) scoring; zero-shot, temperature 0, averaged over 3 runs.
contributions.evaluation: GPT-4 scores 69.9 EM / 82.3 F1 on Wikipedia factual data but drops sharply on 2-hop counterfactual (53.1 EM), and lower on 3-hop/4-hop; consistent gap across models, attributed to contamination.
contributions.source_quote: Our experimental results reveal a significant performance gap of several LLMs between Wikipedia-based factual data and counterfactua1 data,deeming data contamination issues in existing benchmarks.

contributions.purpose: Show that final-answer accuracy overstates reasoning: LLMs often reach answers without following the correct reasoning chain.
contributions.mechanism: Reasoning-chain evaluation computing the proportion of correct vs incorrect chains over sub-questions (2^(N+1) possible chains for an N-hop question) and joint-chain EM/F1 (negative-log) scores; manual error analysis of correct/incorrect final answers.
contributions.evaluation: GPT-4 achieves only 36.3% correct reasoning chains across the dataset; GPT-3.5's correct chains only 13.3% while total failure cases reach 69%. Joint reasoning-chain performance degrades sharply as hops increase (e.g. Bing Chat 2-hop vs 3/4-hop). ~4/20 correct final answers came from incorrect chains (bypassing).
contributions.source_quote: Moreover, we observe that LLMs usually bypass the correct re asoning chain, showing an inflated multi-step reasoning performance.

self_declared_provenance.quote: we call our dataset CofCA ... and an equal amount of factual MHQA data from HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA and MuSiQue as the control group.

Hua et al. (2024) introduces a novel benchmark for counterfactual QA tasks by editing six common reasoning schemes in the real world, while still lacking muti-step reasoning evaluation for LLMs. Our work is different from such works in two main aspects: 1) a comprehensive reasoning chain evaluation; and 2) Counterfactual Question Answering that reduces the risk of data contamination.
To interpret the behavior of existing LLMs on each hop of the reasoning process ... we followed the experiment setting proposed by (Tang et al., 2021).

notes: Whole paper is built around negative/critical findings (a project signal): SOTA LLMs' multi-hop QA scores are 'inflated' by contamination and by reasoning-chain bypassing. Strong negative results: large EM/F1 drop factual->counterfactual (GPT-4 69.9->53.1 EM at 2-hop, worse at 3/4-hop); only 36.3% correct reasoning chains for GPT-4, 13.3% for GPT-3.5 with 69% total failures; cliff-like degradation across hops and sub-questions. Nuanced/mixed finding: sub-questions in the prompt help final-QA but the paper notes cases where adding sub-questions decreased GPT-4 F1/EM by 2.5 and 9.4 on 2-hop. Two-stage counterfactual annotation both cause performance drops. GPT-4 better on bridge than comparison questions.
